suggestions.assertion: Creates exactly one dated Daily Handoff file under docs/handoffs/ matching YYYY-MM-DD_NNN_<scope>-handoff.md
suggestions.reason: This passes on filename shape alone — an empty or one-paragraph file with the right name would also pass. The content assertions carry the real weight here, but consider adding a minimum-substance check (e.g. the file must contain the numbered sections the skill prescribes) so filename compliance can't stand in for a real handoff.

suggestions.assertion: Uncommitted working-tree state recorded (nothing was committed this session)
suggestions.reason: A vague sentence like 'nothing was committed today' satisfies this, which is weak because the transcript already hands that fact over verbatim. The discriminating version requires repo-derived specifics — branch name, HEAD sha, and the actual untracked paths from git status — which is what this run produced (feat/auth-rebuild @ 7991fb7, ?? src/auth/, ?? migrations/) and which a skill that merely paraphrases the transcript could not produce.

No assertion rewards grounding the handoff in the repo rather than only in the transcript, yet that was the most valuable thing this run did: it caught that vitest is referenced by package.json's test script but never declared as a dependency, that SESSION_SECRET falls back to a hardcoded 'dev-only-secret', that docs/ARCHITECTURE.md line 4 still says the session-storage decision is open, and that neither docs/SPEC.md nor docs/SPEC-v1.md actually exists in the repo. Consider an assertion like 'handoff cites at least one file/line-level fact verifiable in the repo but absent from the transcript'.

CSRF handling is stated in the transcript as the explicit, accepted cost of choosing the cookie (line 15) and nothing was built for it. That is a real unblocked carry-forward with no assertion covering it. A skill could pass all 14 current assertions while dropping it entirely.

Nothing tests the anti-fabrication edge that this fixture is built to probe from the other direction — e.g. an assertion that the handoff does NOT claim tests passed, a build/typecheck ran, or the staging migration was applied. Assertions 3 and 10 approach this but are phrased as presence-of-open-item rather than absence-of-false-claim, so a handoff that both lists the tests as open and elsewhere says 'verified working' would still pass.

The prompt's stated goal is 'pick this straight back up tomorrow morning without rereading any of it', but no assertion covers usability. The output is ~29k chars across 11 sections — complete and accurate, yet arguably longer than the raw 78-line transcript it replaces. If concision or a scannable top-of-file summary matters to this skill, it needs its own assertion; if it deliberately does not, that's worth noting so length is never read as a defect.

eval_feedback.overall: Strong, well-targeted assertion set — each of the 14 maps to a specific fidelity trap in the fixture (validated vs unvalidated, parked vs done, local vs staging, rejected option named, blocker owner). All 14 pass on genuine substance, and independent repo inspection confirmed every factual claim I could check with zero fabrications. The main gaps are structural rather than substantive: assertions 1 and 14 are satisfiable too cheaply, and three real outcomes (CSRF debt, repo-grounded discoveries, absence-of-false-claims) go unchecked.
